what_its_for: Butenafine is an antifungal cream used to treat fungal skin infections. It works against athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris), and ringworm (tinea corporis). It kills the fungus causing your skin infection by stopping it from growing.
how_to_take: Butenafine is applied directly to the skin as a cream. Before applying, wash and completely dry the affected area. Apply a thin layer of the cream to the infected skin and a small area around it. Rub it in gently. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream unless your hands are the area being treated. Do not cover the area with bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. Keep the cream away from your eyes, nose, mouth, and vaginal area. This medicine is for skin use only — do not swallow it.
dosing: For athlete's foot between the toes: Apply once a day for 7 days, OR once a day for 4 weeks, depending on the product label or your doctor's instructions. For athlete's foot on the bottom or sides of feet, jock itch, or ringworm: Apply once a day for 2 weeks. Always follow the directions on your product label or what your doctor tells you. Do not use more than directed.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Try to apply it at the same time each day to help you remember.
storage: Store butenafine cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze the cream. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not get butenafine cream in your eyes, mouth, nose, or vagina. Avoid covering the treated area with tight or non-breathable clothing or bandages unless your doctor tells you to. Do not stop using the cream early even if your skin looks better — stopping too soon can let the fungus come back. Avoid sharing towels, socks, or shoes with others while being treated, as fungal infections can spread. Keep the affected area clean and dry as much as possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or pharmacist if: your skin gets worse or you develop increased redness, itching, burning, blistering, swelling, or oozing after starting the cream; your infection does not improve after 2 to 4 weeks of treatment; you develop a skin rash or signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face or throat — this is a medical emergency, call 911 immediately; you accidentally swallow any of the cream.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief from itching and discomfort within a few days of starting treatment. However, the full effect takes longer. For athlete's foot and ringworm, it may take 2 to 4 weeks to fully clear the infection. For jock itch, improvement is often seen within 2 weeks. It is very important to finish the entire course of treatment even if your skin feels better, to make sure the fungus is completely gone and does not come back.
special_populations: Children: Butenafine cream (over-the-counter) is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age without a doctor's guidance. Ask your child's doctor before use. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using butenafine. It is not fully known how this medicine may affect an unborn baby or nursing infant. If breastfeeding, do not apply the cream to the breast or nipple area. Elderly patients: No special dosage adjustments are typically needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's advice.
